generated by `scripts/build-metadata.ps1`. The table below summarizes the intent structure:

| Intent | Canonical Skill | Agent | Example Phrases |
|--------|----------------|-------|-----------------|
| `wireframe-a-flow` | wireframing | @ux-designer | "wireframe onboarding", "lo-fi sketch for checkout" |
| `debate-design-options` | design-debate | @design-reviewer | "compare options", "ADR for navigation", "tradeoff analysis" |
| `audit-accessibility` | accessibility-audit | @accessibility-auditor | "WCAG audit", "a11y review", "aria label check" |
| `design-token-schema` | design-tokens | @design-system-architect | "token architecture", "semantic alias design", "dark-mode tokens" |
| `brand-identity-review` | brand-identity | @brand-steward | "logo usage", "brand guideline", "visual identity" |
| `ia-taxonomy-design` | taxonomy | @information-architect | "taxonomy for nav", "ontology model", "content hierarchy" |
| `craft-critique` | craft-quality | @design-reviewer | "craft bar review", "polish pass", "design critique" |
| `color-system-design` | color-system | @design-system-architect | "color palette", "contrast-safe hues", "semantic color" |
| `responsive-layout` | responsive-design | @ux-designer | "mobile breakpoints", "fluid grid", "responsive patterns" |
| `style-guide-authoring` | style-guide-authoring | @design-reviewer | "document the style guide", "component spec page" |
| `usability-test-mapping` | usability-mapping | @accessibility-auditor | "map usability risk", "usability score", "heuristic check" |

## Machine-Readable Vocabulary

`sheen.vocab.yaml` at the repository root contains the machine-readable intent → skill → agent mapping.
Generated by `scripts/build-metadata.ps1`. Add new intents there (not here) when authoring new skills.
Validated by the `catalog-drift` gate in `checks.json`.

## Router Governance

- Maintain keyword uniqueness — no keyword maps to more than one agent within the sheen pillar table.
- When adding a new skill, register its intent in `sheen.vocab.yaml` via `build-metadata.ps1`.
- The router must not modify agent or skill files — it reads and delegates only.
- Cross-pillar requests (e.g., brand token design) → prefer the agent whose pillar owns the **output artifact**, then compose the second agent as a reviewer.
- Sheen router governs design-domain only. Route engineering, security, and DevOps requests to `/basecoat`.

## Basecoat Cross-Repo Delegate Entry

For the basecoat governance table (`vendor/` excluded), the following entry registers sheen as a delegate:

```markdown
| ux, design, brand, a11y, token, wireframe | @sheen-router | 🎨 Design (→ sheen) |
```

Until that PR lands in basecoat, `/basecoat ux` falls through to basecoat's own `@ux-designer`
(different agent, narrower scope). Document this gap in sheen's CONTRIBUTING.md.
